cut_items.item: Explains why the rejection happens: after a rebase the local history no longer extends the remote history
Command `git log HEAD..origin/your-branch` to specifically show unfetched remote commits not in local branch
Open pull request is updated by the push, but review comments on old commits may become outdated
Alternative: merge the target branch into the feature branch instead of rebasing, which pushes without force but adds a merge commit
Warns that a plain git pull by teammates would merge old and new history together (explains why reset is needed)
Specific check command `git log HEAD..origin/your-branch` showing only remote commits not in local history, which more precisely detects others' commits
Warning that if the branch has an open pull request, the force push updates it and review comments on old commits can become outdated
Alternative: merge the target branch into the feature branch instead of rebasing, which pushes without force at the cost of a merge commit
Explains that a normal `git pull` by teammates would merge old and new history together
Explicit full command in a code block with `--force-with-lease` usage

added_items.item: Explicit ordered workflow: fetch, inspect log of origin/your-branch, then push with lease
Says to stop if unrecognized commits are present, because a force push will delete their work (explicit stop instruction)
Advice to tell teammates before force-pushing if they share the branch
Explains why the push is rejected (remote has old commits) and that replacing remote history is the correct fix
Explicit step to run `git fetch origin` and `git log origin/your-branch` to verify commits before pushing
